record.original_question: What is the minimax memory-bounded first-order oracle complexity T_{L,B}(d,M,epsilon) for minimizing a convex L-Lipschitz function F:R^d->R over the Euclidean ball {x: ||x|| <= B} when there exists an optimizer x* with ||x*|| <= B, and an algorithm is allowed T exact first-order oracle calls that each reveal F(x) and a subgradient at x but only M bits of state may be stored between oracle accesses? Equivalently, which query-memory pairs (T,M) are possible or impossible for this problem, preferably up to constant factors and at worst up to polylogarithmic factors in T and M?

evidence.quote: We define the minimax memory-bounded first-order oracle complexity as TL,B(d, M, epsilon) = inf { T in N : inf_{A in A_{M,T}} sup_{F in F^d_{L,B}} F(A(F)) - min_{||x||<=B} F(x) <= epsilon }.

Question 1 ($500 or Two Star Michelin Meal) Provide a complete characterization of T(d, M, epsilon) and the possible (T, M) trade-off, preferably up to constant factors, and at most up to factors poly-logarithmic in T and M.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$, $L, B > 0$, and $\varepsilon > 0$. Let $\mathcal{F}^d_{L,B}$ denote the class of convex, $L$-Lipschitz functions $F:\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ that attain their minimum over the Euclidean ball $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^d : \|x\| \le B\}$ at some point $x^*$ with $\|x^*\| \le B$.

A memory-bounded first-order optimization algorithm with $T$ queries and $M$ bits of memory is specified as follows: at each round $t = 1, \dots, T$, the algorithm chooses a query point $x_t \in \mathbb{R}^d$ as a (possibly randomized) function of its current memory state $S_{t-1} \in \{0,1\}^M$; it then receives from an exact first-order oracle the pair $(F(x_t), g_t)$ where $g_t \in \partial F(x_t)$; finally it updates the memory state to $S_t \in \{0,1\}^M$ as a (possibly randomized) function of $S_{t-1}$ and $(F(x_t), g_t)$. After $T$ rounds the algorithm outputs a point $A(F) \in \mathbb{R}^d$ as a function of $S_T$. Let $\mathcal{A}_{M,T}$ denote the class of all such algorithms.

Define the minimax memory-bounded first-order oracle complexity
$$T_{L,B}(d, M, \varepsilon) \;=\; \inf\Big\{ T \in \mathbb{N} \;:\; \inf_{A \in \mathcal{A}_{M,T}} \sup_{F \in \mathcal{F}^d_{L,B}} \mathbb{E}\big[F(A(F))\big] - \min_{\|x\|\le B} F(x) \;\le\; \varepsilon \Big\}.$$

Provide a complete characterization of $T_{L,B}(d, M, \varepsilon)$ and of the set of achievable pairs $(T,M)$, preferably up to constant factors and at worst up to factors poly-logarithmic in $T$ and $M$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been partially resolved but not fully characterized. Marsden, Sharan, Sidford, and Valiant (2022) proved the first nontrivial lower bound, showing that any first-order algorithm using at most $d^{1.25-\delta}$ bits of memory needs $\Omega(d^{1+(4/3)\delta})$ queries to minimize 1-Lipschitz convex functions over the unit ball to $1/\mathrm{poly}(d)$ accuracy. Subsequent work by Blanchard, Zhang, and Jaillet (2023) strengthened this, showing that quadratic memory is necessary to achieve the optimal $\widetilde{O}(d)$ query complexity of cutting-plane methods, establishing center-of-mass as Pareto-optimal at one endpoint. A complete tight characterization of the full $(T, M)$ trade-off curve up to constant or polylogarithmic factors remains open.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Convex Optimization Requires Superlinear Memory
status_evidence.snippet: Any memory-constrained, first-order algorithm which minimizes d-dimensional, 1-Lipschitz convex functions over the unit ball to 1/poly(d) accuracy using at most d^(1.25-δ) bits of memory must make at least Ω(d^(1+(4/3)δ)) first-order queries.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the first nontrivial memory-query lower bound, partially resolving the open problem.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Memory is Necessary for Optimal Query Complexity in Convex Optimization: Center-of-Mass is Pareto-Optimal
status_evidence.snippet: Quadratic memory is necessary to match the optimal query complexity achieved by cutting-plane methods; center-of-mass is Pareto-optimal at this endpoint.
status_evidence.claim: Tightens the tradeoff at the high-memory end but does not give a complete characterization of all (T,M) pairs.

status_evidence.title: Memory-Query Tradeoffs for Randomized Convex Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Studies randomized memory-query tradeoffs for convex optimization, providing further partial progress.
status_evidence.claim: Additional partial progress on the tradeoff but no complete characterization.
